1. Case 1: Sneddon-Wilkinson disease
Annular scaly plaques with pustules and central clearing initially suggested dermatophyte infection, but terbinafine/miconazole failed. This refutes fungal infection and supports an inflammatory pustular dermatosis, which the pathologist favors as Sneddon-Wilkinson disease. DIF, desmoglein/IgA anti-desmocollin, and SPEP/immunofixation remain unretrieved, so IgA pemphigus and paraproteinemic subcorneal pustulosis are not fully excluded, but histology makes Sneddon-Wilkinson disease the leading diagnosis.
